text.p: Troubled oil refiner Mazheikiu Nafta said on Wednesday that it was more optimistic about 1997 after making net losses in 1996 of 17.79 million litas.
The 1996 loss was a slight improvement on 1995, when it made a 32.86 million litas loss.
"We expect that 1997 will be more successful for Mazheikiu Nafta," company director general Gediminas Kiesus said in a statement issued as it held its annual shareholder meeting.
He said the company would be able to operate more successfully as it had acquired capital with which to buy crude oil for refining.
Mazheikiu suffers from persistent stoppages and last year had to halt work for 81 days, compared with 130 days in 1995.
The company's turnover in 1996 rose to 998.1 million litas from 930 million litas in 1995. Gross profit tripled in 1996 to 190.05 million litas versus 60.7 million litas a year before.
But it had an operating loss of 14.2 million litas versus a 53.2 million litas loss a year before.
Total assets at the end of 1996 were 852.84 million litas versus 917.87 million litas in 1995.

"The initiative of Mazheikiu Nafta to seek credits, the issue of securities, the upgrading of technological processes and the development of a filling station network provides a realistic hope that the most difficult stage of the company is behind us," Kiesus added.
The government owns 90.5 percent of the comany and the rest is owned by local investors.
In January, the governement decided to merge the four big oil companies, Mazheikiu Nafta, Lietuvos Kuras, Butinge Nafta and Naftotiekis into a national oil company, Lietuvos Nafta.
Mazheikiu plans to start implementing a $100 million investment program in the second half of 1997 by upgrading its production lines.
